s1.p27: So, there are a few ‘shortcomings’ of timers that make it undesirable to use them for animation.
s1.p28: The first is that you can never be sure that the time that passes until the timer's callback function enters the Call Stack will be the time you set when you set the timer.
s1.p29: The second is that it is completely unrealistic to match the frequency at which the browser redraws the page with the frequency at which the timer's callback is called.

s1.p42: Debounce is an unpleasant phenomenon which means that some function is called too often.
s1.p43: This happens most frequently with UI event handlers.
s1.p44: It is especially bad if the function code sends a request to the server.
s1.p45: It takes time to process such a request, and an impatient user may repeatedly press the button without waiting for an immediate response.
s1.p46: Also debounce can occur due to technical reasons, for example, when a mouse button or a key on the keyboard ‘sticks’.
s1.p47: Our task is to prevent debounce regardless of the reason of its origin, i.e. ‘throttle’ function calls by controlling their frequency.
